answers.docs.gaps:
1. Tabular min-width. docs/crates/render/guides/intro-to-tabular.md, Step 4: `{"min": 10}` =
   "At least 10, grows to fit content". Since `t.row(...)` formats one row at a time, there is no
   whole-table measurement; with `{"min": 0}` on three columns I got the collapsed layout quoted in
   my friction answer, not columns sized to the widest cell. The guide never says the growth is
   per-row, nor how to get a table sized to its data from a template.

2. Trailing newlines are undocumented. docs/topics/execution-outcomes.md covers streams and statuses
   for the final write but never says the renderer drops the template's last newline and the
   framework appends one. That is load-bearing for any byte-exact output contract.

3. `#[dispatch(pure)]` is used in three separate examples and defined nowhere in docs/.

4. The nested `#[derive(Dispatch)]` example in docs/topics/app-configuration.md ("From Dispatch
   Macro") does not compile as written: it lacks the `#[dispatch(handlers = ...)]` attribute the
   macro requires.

5. Template resolution for nested command groups is not documented. docs/topics/app-configuration.md
   says templates are "referenced by path without extension: `"list"`, `"db/migrate"`" for the
   builder API, but for `#[dispatch(nested)]` enums nothing states what template name a command path
   like `pr checks list` resolves to. I guessed `src/templates/pr/checks/list.jinja` and it worked.

6. `.commands(Commands::dispatch_config())?` vs `.commands(Commands::dispatch_config()?)` — the two
   guides contradict each other (see friction #3).
answers.friction:
1. `#[dispatch(pure)]` appears on every command variant in docs/index.md,
   docs/guides/minimal-single-crate.md, and docs/guides/intro-to-standout.md, but nothing in docs/
   says what it means. I copied it because the examples do.

2. The nested-enum example in docs/topics/app-configuration.md:

       #[derive(Dispatch)]
       enum Commands {
           List,
           Add,
           #[dispatch(nested)]
           Db(DbCommands),
       }

   My equivalent root enum (all variants `#[dispatch(nested)]`) failed to compile:

       error: missing `#[dispatch(handlers = path)]` attribute
         --> src/commands.rs:15:1

   Adding `#[dispatch(handlers = crate::handlers)]` to an enum with no non-nested variants fixed it.

3. Two docs pages disagree about `dispatch_config()`'s shape:
   docs/guides/minimal-single-crate.md has `.commands(Commands::dispatch_config())?` while
   docs/guides/tldr-intro-to-standout.md has `.commands(Commands::dispatch_config()?)`. The first is
   the one that compiles.

4. Nothing in docs/ describes trailing-newline handling, and the spec's expected output is
   byte-exact, so I had to probe it: a template file containing `A` produced `A\n`, `A\n\n`
   produced `A\n\n`, and my first `pr list` template produced a spurious blank final line. The
   effective rule is that the template's own final newline is dropped and the framework appends
   exactly one, so a loop must emit the newline *before* each row rather than after it.

5. `tabular()` with data-driven widths did not lay out a table. Per
   docs/crates/render/guides/intro-to-tabular.md, `{"min": 10}` means "At least 10, grows to fit
   content", so I tried three `{"width": {"min": 0}}` columns with `t.row(...)` per row and got:

         STATE                                                       (padded to terminal width)
         open
         merged

   i.e. the first two columns collapsed and the last one absorbed the terminal width. I fell back to
   the `col` filter with widths computed in the template.

6. docs/topics/error-handling.md says ordinary handler errors get "the normal handler diagnostic
   framing" but never shows that framing, so I could not tell from docs whether a bare
   `ghlike: repository not found: demo/gamma` line on stderr was reachable that way. I used
   `ExternalFailure`, which docs do specify as verbatim ("Standout adds no `Error:` prefix and no
   trailing newline").

answers.summary:
Built `ghlike`, a single-crate standout 8.1.1 CLI in `app/`, complete and passing every
behavior in SPEC.md. Layout: `src/forge.rs` (CLI-free frozen state + lookups), `src/view.rs`
(serializable view DTOs), `src/json.rs` (`--json` field selection and compact JSON emission),
`src/commands.rs` (clap derive tree + `#[derive(Dispatch)]`, nested for `auth`/`repo`/`pr` and
`pr checks`), `src/handlers.rs` (`#[handler]` adapters), `src/templates/**.jinja`, `src/styles/default.css`.

Human output goes through templates (column widths computed in-template with
`display_width`/`max` and the `col` filter, so each column but the last is padded to its widest
rendered cell, header included when shown) and is styled on an attended terminal. `--json <fields>`
returns `Output::Binary`, so the bytes on stdout are exactly the compact JSON document (fields in
the requested order, `number` a number, `draft` a boolean) with no styling, paging, or prose in any
terminal. Domain errors (unknown repo, unknown PR, unknown `--json` field) exit 1 with empty stdout
and the exact stderr line; usage errors (group without subcommand, unknown subcommand or flag) exit
2 via clap; `--help` exits 0 on stdout at every level.

`cargo build`, `cargo build --release`, and `cargo test` (11 unit tests: core lookups, JSON
projection, handler adapters) all succeed. I verified the built binary against every example and
error case in SPEC.md with a script that compares exit status, stdout, and stderr byte for byte:
17/17 cases match, plus checks that all three group-without-subcommand invocations exit 2 with
empty stdout and guidance on stderr, and that `--help` at all ten levels exits 0 with clean stderr.
answers.workarounds:
1. `ExternalFailure` for ordinary domain errors. docs/topics/error-handling.md says "Use
   `ExternalFailure` only when another operation owns the status and diagnostic contract, such as a
   delegated Git invocation", and no external process is involved here. I use it in
   `handlers::domain_failure` because it is the only documented seam that yields exit 1 with a
   verbatim stderr payload, which SPEC.md requires. If Standout ever gains a first-class way to
   declare an application's own exit status and diagnostic text, that is the seam this should move to.

2. `Output::Binary` for `--json`. The `--json <fields>` payload is emitted as bytes rather than
   `Output::Render`, so it bypasses the template and the BBCode pass entirely. That is what
   guarantees "never styled, never framed" even on a color-capable terminal — a JSON array starts
   with `[{`, and the BBCode pass marks unknown tags with `?` in terminal mode, so rendering JSON
   through a template would have risked corrupting it. It also keeps field order and compactness
   under my control (structured `--output json` would serialize the view DTO instead, alphabetically
   and pretty-printed). The handler branches on an explicit argument, not on output mode.

3. Column widths are computed inside the templates
   (`(["NUMBER"] + (pull_requests | map(attribute="number") | map("string") | list)) |
   map("display_width") | max`) and applied with `col(width)`, instead of `tabular()`/`table()`,
   because of gap #1. Padding still lives in the presentation layer, not in handlers.

4. `#![allow(non_snake_case)]` at the top of `src/handlers.rs` to silence 10 warnings about the
   `list__handler` / `list__expected_args` functions the `#[handler]` macro generates.

5. `pr view <number>` and `pr checks list <number>` take the number as a `String` and look it up as
   typed, so `ghlike pr view abc` is `ghlike: no pull request found: abc` (exit 1, a domain error)
   rather than a clap parse failure (exit 2). SPEC.md reserves exit 2 for group-without-subcommand
   and unknown subcommands or flags, so this keeps the two classes apart.

6. `ghlike pr checks list <unknown number>` is not specified; I treat it as the same domain error as
   `pr view` (exit 1, `ghlike: no pull request found: <number>`). PR 3, which exists with no checks,
   prints nothing and exits 0, and `--json` for it emits `[]`.
